Total fees: ~$0.027 across 12 fills.

### What went wrong

1. **Chasing momentum at the top.** Most entries caught the tail end of moves that were already well underway (+24–28% 24h). Only Hua Hong cleared above my entry — the auction happened to print favorably. The others drifted down immediately after entry.

2. **Fee drag kills micro-scalps.** Round-trip fees (~$0.0045) on $5 positions held for 2–3 minutes is brutal. Price moves of $0.01–0.03 per unit don't overcome the spread + fees at this size and frequency.

3. **Thin books on smaller markets.** Biren Technology had no fill at all. Sticking to the most-traded names (NVDA, QQQ, SPY) would have given better execution.

4. **Short timing was poor.** SONY looked like it was accelerating down (-1.38%), but it bounced right after I entered the short.

5. **Holding periods too short.** The strategy demanded trades every 2 min, but meaningful price movement on these markets needs longer. The one winner (Hua Hong) was held the longest (~4 min) and benefited from auction pricing luck more than signal.

**Bottom line:** Lost $0.04 on $18.87 (-0.2%). The win on Hua Hong nearly offset everything, but frequent rotation into new positions just generated fees without enough edge to cover them.
